newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai shares down at noon on quota, off lows.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai shares down at noon on quota, off lows.

text.p: Shanghai's A and B shares were down at noon on Friday after Beijing announced a huge new quota for stock issues in 1997, but the indices were off intraday lows with investors recovering from the shock quickly, traders said.
Shanghai's B share index fell 1.491 points or 1.68 percent to 87.279 at midday after hitting a low of 86.246 points in early trade. Volume was 9.0 million shares worth $6.5 million.
The A share index shed 33.578 points or 2.26 percent to 1,449.665 after hitting a low of 1,361,895 points. Volume was 413.1 million shares worth 5.8 billion yuan.

The Securities Commission under the State Council (cabinet) and the State Planning Commission on Thursday announced a quota for new stock issues in 1997 of 30 billion yuan, compared with the 1996 quota of 15 billion.
Brokers said the market had been unprepared for such a huge quota and did not expect Beijing to announce the year's quota so soon. China usually announces a year's quota at the end of the year.
"Investors were caught completely unprepared," said one broker. "This caused panic selling in the first few minutes of trading."
But the indices quickly began to trim losses partly due to strong market fundamentals and a belief that market expansion would be beneficial in the long run, broker said.
"Investors quickly recovered from the shock," said a second broker. "The potential for further losses will be limited barring fresh negative factors because of the strong fundamentals."
Brokers said the B share index would text the key 87-point support level this afternoon. If the index could stand above the level, the B market will rebound next week.
On the B share market China First Pencil Co was the biggest loser this morning on speculative selling, slipping $0.038 or 7.19 percent to 0.490 on volume of 16,100 shares.

Market barometer Shanghai Lujiazui Finance and Trade Zone Development Co was the most actively traded and fell on heavy selling by retail investors despite institutional support, brokers said. The stock lost $0.016 or 1.10 percent to $1.434 on volume of 1.6 million shares.
On the A market, the SSE 30 blue-chip index dipped 88.359 points or 2.17 percent to 3,989.118 points. Shanghai Fello Co lost 1.84 yuan at its limit-down level of 16.55.
